cards.explanation: The answer is an angel, friends. God says, “Behold, I am sending an angel before you to protect you along the way…” (Exodus 23:20). Out front, watching over the road. I think that's a mighty good traveling companion.

The answer is True. The angel isn't just tagging along, friends. God says he is there “…to bring you to the place I have prepared.” (Exodus 23:20). The place is already prepared, and the angel is the one who leads them there.

The reason is that the angel will not forgive rebellion. God says, “do not defy him, for he will not forgive rebellion, since My Name is in him.” (Exodus 23:21). He gives the reason right there in the verse. This is a messenger to take seriously, friends.

The answer is True, bakers. God tells Israel, “do not defy him, for he will not forgive rebellion, since My Name is in him.” (Exodus 23:21). His Name is in the angel, and that's why the warning is so serious. When this messenger speaks, Israel is told to listen.

The answer is to listen carefully to the angel and obey God fully. God says, “But if you will listen carefully to his voice and do everything I say, I will be an enemy to your enemies and a foe to your foes.” (Exodus 23:22). Listening to the angel and doing everything God says go together, friends. The promise comes with that “if.”

The answer is False. God says, “You must not bow down to their gods or serve them or follow their practices.” (Exodus 23:24). Following their practices is on the list too, friends. It isn't an exception.

The answer is to demolish them and smash their sacred stones, friends! After telling Israel not to bow down to those gods, God says, “Instead, you are to demolish them and smash their sacred stones to pieces.” (Exodus 23:24). I stamp cookies for a living, so swinging a hammer is WAY outside my lane. My biggest demolition job was a tower of cookie boxes I stacked too high. The instruction here is plain, though: those gods are not to be left standing.

The answer is sickness, bakers. God says, “So you shall serve the LORD your God, and He will bless your bread and your water. And I will take away sickness from among you.” (Exodus 23:25). The blessing and the promise come right after serving Him.

The answer is that the enemies turn and run, friends. God says, “I will send My terror ahead of you and throw into confusion every nation you encounter. I will make all your enemies turn and run.” (Exodus 23:27). Terror goes ahead, confusion hits every nation Israel encounters, and the enemies turn and run. That's one way to clear a path.

The answer is the hornet, friends. God says, “I will send the hornet before you to drive the Hivites and Canaanites and Hittites out of your way.” (Exodus 23:28). Small creature, big job. I'm not here to argue with it.

The answer is fruitful, bakers. God says, “Little by little I will drive them out ahead of you, until you become fruitful and possess the land.” (Exodus 23:30). The pace is slow on purpose. Israel grows fruitful while the land becomes theirs.

The answer is True, friends. God says, “For I will deliver the inhabitants into your hand, and you will drive them out before you.” (Exodus 23:31). He delivers them into Israel's hand, and Israel drives them out. Both parts sit in the same verse.

The answer is FALSE, friends, and no loophole is given. God says, “You shall make no covenant with them or with their gods.” (Exodus 23:32). Look at that “or.” The covenant is off the table with the nations and with their gods, not just one of them. The next verse gives a reason: if they stay, they might cause Israel to sin against Him, and serving their gods would be a snare (Exodus 23:33).

The reason God gives is that they would cause Israel to sin against Him, friends. “They must not remain in your land, lest they cause you to sin against Me.” (Exodus 23:33). He adds that serving their gods would surely be a snare. The concern is about sin against Him.
